before.known: he found it unusual to make that choice
before.target: han synes det var usædvanligt at træffe det valg

after.target: han syntes det var usædvanligt at træffe det valg

problem: Grammar/meaning: Danish 'synes' is present tense but the English is past.
evidence: The sibling S0124L01 uses 'syntes' for past 'thought/found'.

before.known: she said it felt unusual
before.target: hun sagde at det føles usædvanligt

problem: Tense mismatch: English 'felt' vs Danish 'føles' (present).
evidence: The target is present tense and no past form of 'føles' is taught.

before.known: he said it felt good to relax
before.target: han sagde at det føles godt at slappe af

after.known: he said it feels good to relax

problem: Tense mismatch: English 'felt' vs Danish 'føles' (present).
evidence: No past form of 'føles' is taught.

before.known: learning a language feels exciting
before.target: at lære et nyt sprog føles interessant

after.known: learning a new language feels interesting

problem: Meaning: English 'exciting' is rendered as 'interessant', and 'new' is added to the Danish only.
evidence: 'spændende' is not taught until seed 132.

before.known: he was excited about the conversation
before.target: han var begejstret for at have en samtale

after.known: he was excited about having a conversation

problem: Meaning: 'the conversation' is rendered as 'at have en samtale'.
evidence: The Danish target says 'having a conversation'.

before.known: she has a good idea about how to learn
before.target: hun synes det er en god idé at lære dansk

problem: Meaning: the English 'has a good idea about how to learn' is mistranslated as 'synes det er en god idé at lære dansk'.
evidence: The Danish adds 'Danish' and changes the sense to an opinion.

before.known: he believes you can learn more quickly
before.target: han tror at du kan lære hurtigt

after.known: he believes you can learn quickly

problem: Meaning: the English says 'more quickly' but the Danish says 'hurtigt'.
evidence: The Danish has no 'mere'.

before.known: she believes learning changes your brain
before.target: hun tror at det at lære ændrer vores hjerne

after.known: she believes learning changes our brain

problem: Meaning: English 'your brain' vs Danish 'vores hjerne' ('our').
evidence: The Danish is 'vores hjerne'.

before.known: learning changes the shape of your thinking
before.target: at lære ændrer formen på hvad du synes

problem: Meaning: 'the shape of your thinking' is rendered as 'formen på hvad du synes', which is wrong and unnatural.
evidence: The Danish says 'the shape of what you think'.

before.known: she wanted to see how it changed
before.target: hun ville se hvordan det ændrer sig

after.known: she wanted to see how it changes

problem: Tense mismatch: English 'changed' vs Danish 'ændrer' (present).
evidence: The Danish verb is present tense.

before.known: did you want to see how it works?
before.target: ville du gerne se hvordan man gør?

after.target: ville du gerne se hvordan det virker?

problem: Meaning: 'how it works' is rendered as 'hvordan man gør' ('how one does').
evidence: 'virker' is available.

before.known: I was excited about the surprise
before.target: jeg var begejstret for en overraskelse

after.known: I was excited about a surprise

problem: Meaning: English 'the surprise' vs Danish 'en overraskelse' ('a surprise').
evidence: The Danish uses the indefinite article.

before.known: so many things are going around in my head
before.target: så mange ting er i mit hoved

problem: Meaning: the English 'going around' is missing from the Danish.
evidence: The Danish is 'så mange ting er i mit hoved'.

before.known: he couldn't stop what was in my head
before.target: han kunne ikke stoppe hvad der er i mit hoved

after.known: he couldn't stop what is in my head

problem: Tense mismatch: English 'was' vs Danish 'er'. The sentence is also clunky.
evidence: The Danish verb is present.

before.known: there are so many things going around in our heads
before.target: der er så mange ting der løber rundt i mit hoved

after.known: there are so many things going around in my head

problem: Meaning: English 'our heads' vs Danish 'mit hoved' ('my head').
evidence: The Danish is singular and first person.

before.known: he said everything was going around
before.target: han sagde at alt løber rundt i mit hoved

problem: Meaning: the English lacks 'in my head' but the Danish adds it.
evidence: The Danish is 'alt løber rundt i mit hoved'.

before.known: she thought the idea was exciting
before.target: hun syntes at det var spændende med en god idé

after.target: hun syntes at det var spændende

problem: Meaning: the Danish 'spændende med en god idé' differs from 'the idea was exciting'.
evidence: The Danish is a different sentence from the English.

before.known: she wanted to get to know the new person
before.target: hun ville gerne lære nogen at kende

after.known: she wanted to get to know someone

problem: Meaning: English 'the new person' vs Danish 'nogen' ('someone').
evidence: The Danish is 'nogen'.

before.known: he hoped to get to know everyone
before.target: han håbede at lære nogen at kende

after.known: he hoped to get to know someone

problem: Meaning: English 'everyone' vs Danish 'nogen' ('someone').
evidence: The Danish is 'nogen'.

before.known: she was excited to get to know new people
before.target: hun var begejstret for at lære nogen at kende

after.known: she was excited to get to know someone

problem: Meaning: English 'new people' vs Danish 'nogen' ('someone').
evidence: The Danish is 'nogen'.

before.known: when you work more you learn more
before.target: når man arbejder mere lærer man meget

after.known: when you work more you learn a lot

problem: Meaning: English 'learn more' vs Danish 'lærer man meget' ('learn a lot').
evidence: The Danish is 'lærer man meget'.

before.known: of course she can ask
before.target: selvfølgelig kan hun spørge hende

after.known: of course she can ask her

problem: Grammar/meaning: the English 'she can ask' has no object but the Danish adds 'hende'. The same subject-object pair also reads as reflexive.
evidence: The Danish is 'selvfølgelig kan hun spørge hende'.

before.known: it's good to practise often
before.target: det er godt at øve mig i at tale ofte

after.known: it's good to practise speaking often

problem: Grammar: 'øve mig' is first person but the English is generic.
evidence: The Danish uses 'mig' in a generic sentence.

before.known: he was surprised to see her so early
before.target: han forventede ikke at se hende så tidligt

after.known: he wasn't expecting to see her so early

problem: Meaning: English 'was surprised' vs Danish 'forventede ikke' ('wasn't expecting').
evidence: The Danish is 'forventede ikke'.
